svg.title: A log-likelihood curve with the cut that defines the interval
svg.desc: The relative log-likelihood for three successes in twenty trials, its quadratic approximation at the maximum, and a horizontal line 1.92 below the peak whose crossings give the interval endpoints.
svg.text: Both intervals are the same cut, taken on two different curves
Relative log-likelihood, meaning the log-likelihood minus its value at the maximum, for three successes in twenty trials.
The two curves agree to second order at the maximum and part company away from it. To the left
the real curve plunges, because a small p makes three successes very unlikely; the parabola does
not know that and crosses the cut at minus 0.006. To the right the real curve sags more gently
than the parabola, so its crossing lands further out, at 0.344 rather than 0.306.
Read the picture as one recipe applied twice. Cut the true curve and you get the
likelihood-ratio interval; cut its quadratic stand-in and you get the Wald interval. They
coincide exactly when the log-likelihood is exactly a parabola.
